summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with psoriatic arthritis and undifferentiated IBD, on long-term immunosuppression with Humira, azathioprine, and prednisone, was admitted for one week of profuse sweating and three days of severe exhaustion. Despite being afebrile, his immunocompromised status prompted an extensive infectious workup, including blood cultures, serologies, lumbar puncture, and imaging (CT chest/abdomen/pelvis, MRI brain), all of which were unremarkable. A right calf lesion was biopsied and found consistent with erythema nodosum, with no evidence of infection. Given the temporal association of symptom onset with his last Humira dose, the medication was discontinued. Azathioprine was held during admission but resumed at discharge, along with prednisone. Trigger point injections were administered for worsening cervical headaches, as Botox was deferred due to diagnostic uncertainty. The patient improved clinically, remained stable, and was discharged home with follow-up arranged in rheumatology and dermatology.
